result.topic_en: Reprinted unsolved questions 1694 and 1695 (Escary, on inequalities and relations involving D, D', m, m', r, r') and the beginning of question 1705 on focal systems and an equilateral paraboloid, with an editorial footnote warning that question 1695 appears to contain errors.
result.transcription:
( 243 )

1694 (1895, 36*). — Démontrer que, dans le cas de $D < D'$, on a l'inégalité
$$\frac{m'D'}{mD} > \frac{r^2}{r'^2} [?] > \frac{m'D}{mD'};$$
et que, si l'on a
$$D > D',$$
la même inégalité a lieu dans un sens opposé. ESCARY.

1695 (1895, 37*). — Sachant qu'on a
$$r''^2 = r^2 + r'^2 + 2rr'\cos(\nu + \nu'),$$
et en posant
$$D^2e^{2\omega} + 1 = P, \qquad D'^2e^{2\omega} + 1 = Q,$$
$$DD'\left(\frac{\sqrt{mD'} + \sqrt{m'D}}{\sqrt{m'D} - \sqrt{mD'}}\right)^2 e^{2\omega} + 1 = S,$$
démontrer les relations suivantes (¹) :
$$r''^2 - \left(\sqrt{\frac{mD}{m'D'}} - 1\right)^2 \frac{S}{P}\, r^2 = \left(\sqrt{\frac{m'D'}{mD}} - 1\right)^2 \frac{S'}{P'}\, r'^2,$$
$$d\xi^2 = \frac{D'^2}{D^2}\,\frac{P^2}{Q^2}\,\frac{e^{2\omega} + D'^2}{e^{2\omega} + D^2}\, d\xi^2,$$
$$d\xi^2 = \frac{D^2}{D'^2}\,\frac{P'}{Q'}\,\frac{e^{2\omega'} + D^2}{e^{2\omega'} + D'^2}\, d\xi'^2.$$
ESCARY.

questions.statement_en: Prove that, in the case $D < D'$, one has the inequality $$\frac{m'D'}{mD} > \frac{r^2}{r'^2} > \frac{m'D}{mD'};$$ and that, if $D > D'$, the same inequality holds in the opposite direction.

questions.author: Escary
questions.statement_fr:
Sachant qu'on a
$$r''^2 = r^2 + r'^2 + 2rr'\cos(\nu + \nu'),$$
et en posant
$$D^2e^{2\omega} + 1 = P, \qquad D'^2e^{2\omega} + 1 = Q,$$
$$DD'\left(\frac{\sqrt{mD'} + \sqrt{m'D}}{\sqrt{m'D} - \sqrt{mD'}}\right)^2 e^{2\omega} + 1 = S,$$
démontrer les relations suivantes :
$$r''^2 - \left(\sqrt{\frac{mD}{m'D'}} - 1\right)^2 \frac{S}{P}\, r^2 = \left(\sqrt{\frac{m'D'}{mD}} - 1\right)^2 \frac{S'}{P'}\, r'^2,$$
$$d\xi^2 = \frac{D'^2}{D^2}\,\frac{P^2}{Q^2}\,\frac{e^{2\omega} + D'^2}{e^{2\omega} + D^2}\, d\xi^2,$$
$$d\xi^2 = \frac{D^2}{D'^2}\,\frac{P'}{Q'}\,\frac{e^{2\omega'} + D^2}{e^{2\omega'} + D'^2}\, d\xi'^2.$$
questions.statement_en: Given that $$r''^2 = r^2 + r'^2 + 2rr'\cos(\nu + \nu'),$$ and setting $$D^2e^{2\omega} + 1 = P, \qquad D'^2e^{2\omega} + 1 = Q,$$ $$DD'\left(\frac{\sqrt{mD'} + \sqrt{m'D}}{\sqrt{m'D} - \sqrt{mD'}}\right)^2 e^{2\omega} + 1 = S,$$ prove the following relations: $$r''^2 - \left(\sqrt{\frac{mD}{m'D'}} - 1\right)^2 \frac{S}{P}\, r^2 = \left(\sqrt{\frac{m'D'}{mD}} - 1\right)^2 \frac{S'}{P'}\, r'^2,$$ $$d\xi^2 = \frac{D'^2}{D^2}\,\frac{P^2}{Q^2}\,\frac{e^{2\omega} + D'^2}{e^{2\omega} + D^2}\, d\xi^2,$$ $$d\xi^2 = \frac{D^2}{D'^2}\,\frac{P'}{Q'}\,\frac{e^{2\omega'} + D^2}{e^{2\omega'} + D'^2}\, d\xi'^2.$$

questions.statement_en:
Consider a given focal system as the union of two reciprocal systems, and rotate one of these systems through a half-turn about a line subject only to the condition of meeting the axis of the focal system at a right angle.
Prove that, in this new position, the two systems are polar reciprocals with respect to an equilateral paraboloid.

result.notes_en: A footnote attached to question 1695 states that several of its formulas appear to contain errors, perhaps typographical, that P', Q', S' were never defined, and that the statement has nonetheless been reproduced exactly as printed in 1895.
